auth.loginSubtitle: Cloud ERP for East African SMEs
auth.forgotSubtitle: We will email you a link to set a new one.
auth.resetRequestedBody: If an account exists for that address, a link to set a new password is on its way. The link expires, so use it soon.
auth.resetSubtitle: This signs you out everywhere else.
auth.passwordsMustMatch: Both passwords must be the same
auth.resetDoneBody: Sign in with your new password.
auth.resetFailed: That link is no longer valid
auth.resetFailedBody: A reset link works once and expires. Ask for a new one and use the most recent email.
auth.verifyDoneBody: Thank you — nothing else to do.
auth.verifyFailed: That link is no longer valid
auth.verifyFailedBody: Verification links work once and expire. Ask for a new one below.
auth.verifyBanner: Your email address is not verified.
auth.verifySentBody: Check your inbox for the link.
auth.verifyAlreadyDone: Your email address is already verified
auth.verifySendFailed: Could not send the verification email
auth.acceptSubtitle: Choose a name and a password, and you are in.
auth.acceptFailed: That invitation is no longer valid
auth.acceptFailedBody: Invitations work once and expire, and a revoked one stops working immediately. Ask whoever invited you to send another.
auth.missingTokenBody: Open the link from your email exactly as it was sent.

errors.unauthenticated: Your session has expired. Please sign in again.
errors.invalid_credentials: That email or password isn't right.
errors.no_membership: You don't have access to that company.
errors.permission_denied: You don't have permission to do that.
errors.unbalanced_entry: Debits and credits must be equal before posting.
errors.period_not_open: That accounting period isn't open for posting.
errors.no_accounting_period: No accounting period covers that date.
errors.missing_exchange_rate: No exchange rate found for that date.
errors.idempotency_key_reused: This document was already submitted with different details.
errors.not_found: That record could not be found.
errors.conflict: That change conflicts with existing data.
errors.account_not_postable: That account can't be posted to directly.
errors.account_in_use: This account is referenced by GL settings and cannot be deactivated.
errors.account_has_non_zero_balance: An account with a non-zero balance cannot be deactivated.
errors.tax_code_has_postings: Tax rate cannot be changed once transactions exist. Add a new tax code.
errors.currency_has_postings: Decimal places cannot be changed once transactions exist in this currency.
errors.control_account_manual_posting: Control accounts can't be posted to manually.
errors.dimension_required: A required field is missing on one of the lines.
errors.dimension_invalid: One of the lines has an invalid branch or project.
errors.too_few_lines: An entry needs at least two lines.
errors.zero_amount_line: Every line needs a non-zero amount.
errors.entry_not_posted: Only posted entries can be reversed.
errors.cannot_reverse_a_reversal: A reversal can't itself be reversed.
errors.entry_already_reversed: This entry has already been reversed.
errors.generic: Something went wrong. Please try again.
errors.pageBody: The page hit an unexpected error. You can try again, or head back to the dashboard.

gl.reverseDescription: This creates a reversing entry dated as below.
gl.projectSubsetNote: Project slice of balanced entries does not foot by design.
gl.noTransactions: No transactions found for this period and filters.
gl.selectAccountToBegin: Select an account to view its ledger transactions.
gl.selectAccountHint: Select an account above to inspect all posted ledger movements and running balance.
gl.noAccountsMatch: No accounts match the current filter.
gl.reverseAlreadyReversed: This entry has already been reversed
gl.reverseModuleOwned: Posted by the {module} module — reverse it from that module's document, so the stock or open items it moved are reversed too

fxRevaluation.title: FX revaluation
fxRevaluation.subtitle: What the open foreign-currency documents are worth at a date
fxRevaluation.previewNote: The revaluation moves the revaluation and unrealized gain/loss accounts. It never touches the receivable or payable control accounts, whose balance is the open items at the rates they were booked at.
fxRevaluation.nothingToRevalue: No open foreign-currency document at this date.
fxRevaluation.postDescription: The run posts an entry at the revaluation date and its mirror the following day, in one transaction.
fxRevaluation.postNote: The balance sheet at the date carries the revaluation; the next period does not. Realized exchange differences at allocation are unaffected.
fxRevaluation.postFailed: The revaluation could not be posted
fxRevaluation.noRuns: No revaluation has been posted for this company.
fxRevaluation.detailDescription: The lines as the run used them — a later correction to an exchange rate does not restate a posted revaluation.
fxRevaluation.reverseReasonPlaceholder: Why this run is being undone
fxRevaluation.reverseFailed: The run could not be reversed

maintenance.name: Name
maintenance.transactionTypesEmpty: No transaction types for this module yet.
maintenance.glTransactionTypesSubtitle: Determination chain rules for General Ledger (ADR-05)
maintenance.arTransactionTypesSubtitle: Determination-chain defaults for customer invoices, credit notes and receipts
maintenance.apTransactionTypesSubtitle: Determination-chain defaults for supplier invoices, debit notes and payments
maintenance.projectsSubtitle: Cross-module job costing and analytics dimension (ADR-04 / D8)
maintenance.defaultsSubtitle: General Ledger default accounts for automated system entries
maintenance.taxesSubtitle: Tax codes, statutory VAT rates, and linked ledger accounts (Appendix C.1)
maintenance.renameAccountSubtitle: Update an account code while keeping its full ledger history and linkages intact
maintenance.renameKeepsHistoryNote: Existing journal lines stay tied to this account; only the visible code is updated.
maintenance.noChangeEvents: No change events recorded for this account.
maintenance.currenciesSubtitle: Currencies and dated exchange rate schedules (ADR-06)
maintenance.chartOfAccountsSubtitle: Tree hierarchy by parent account · {shown} of {total} accounts
maintenance.filterAccountsPlaceholder: Filter accounts by code or name…
maintenance.filterAccountsAria: Filter accounts by code or name
maintenance.noAccountsMatch: No accounts match the current filter.
maintenance.noPeriods: No accounting periods. A company is set up with a financial year, so this is a company that has not finished setting up.
maintenance.generalSettingsSubtitle: Default accounts for year-end retained earnings and FX rounding
maintenance.reopenAuditDescription: Reopening a closed fiscal boundary is audited.
maintenance.usersSubtitle: Manage organization memberships, invitations, and role assignments (ADR-02)
maintenance.chooseTransactionTypeKind: Choose what this type does to stock
maintenance.invTransactionTypesSubtitle: Every inventory document names one of these. The kind says what it does to stock; the default account is the contra the value goes to.
maintenance.revokeInvitationBody: The link in {email}'s invitation stops working immediately. You can invite them again afterwards.
maintenance.ebmTaxClassNote: Which of the authority's four tax classes (A exempt, B standard, C zero-rated, D non-VAT) a line carrying this code is reported under. A fiscalized sale on an unmapped code is refused.
maintenance.defaultPurchaseClassNote: The class a purchase line with no item is registered under — rent, freight, a consultant's fee. The authority requires a class on every line and Vinea does not require an item, so one default bridges the two.
maintenance.taxDefaultsNote: None of these may be a control account, and the revaluation contras are deliberately not the AR/AP control accounts: a control account's balance is the sum of open items at their booking rates, which a revaluation would break.

ar.noHistory: No change events recorded for this customer.
ar.subtitle: Partner master, AR role — settings, credit terms and contacts
ar.onHold: On hold — block new documents for this customer

ap.noHistory: No change events recorded for this supplier.
ap.subtitle: Partner master, AP role — settings, credit terms and contacts
ap.onHold: On hold — block new documents for this supplier

partners.renameHint: Codes change on the <link></link> screen, which keeps the full history.

settings.creditLimit: Credit limit (base currency — blank means no limit, 0 means no credit)

salesReps.title: Sales representatives
salesReps.subtitle: Attributed on customer settings and carried onto AR documents

paymentTerms.title: Payment terms
paymentTerms.subtitle: Due-date basis and the settlement discount, which is taken at allocation — not at invoice time
paymentTerms.discountNote: The discount is taken when you allocate, if the allocation falls inside the discount window. VAT is not adjusted automatically on settlement discounts; issue a credit note where required.

bucketSets.title: Ageing bucket sets
bucketSets.subtitle: Buckets and the ageing basis used by the age analysis — configurable per company
bucketSets.contiguityNote: Buckets start at day 0, run contiguously and the last one stays open-ended.

defaults.title: AR/AP defaults
defaults.subtitle: Control accounts and the automatic postings the subledger makes on your behalf
defaults.controlNote: Control accounts are maintained by the AR and AP subledgers. A manual journal cannot post to one, and every subledger line that touches one records the partner it belongs to.
defaults.fxNote: Posted when you allocate, dated the allocation date, for the difference between the two documents' booking rates in base currency. Both can be the same account.
defaults.discountNote: Posted when you allocate, not when you invoice. VAT is not adjusted automatically on settlement discounts; issue a credit note where required.
defaults.postDatedNote: A receipt or payment with a future maturity date holds its cash here instead of the bank, and moves to the bank on or after that date. You can still allocate it in the meantime.
defaults.readOnlyNote: You can view these defaults but not change them. Changing them needs General Ledger setup permission.

rename.title: Rename customer / supplier code
rename.subtitle: Change a code while every document, allocation and open item keeps its history
rename.safetyNote: Documents, allocations and journal lines stay tied to this partner; only the visible code changes. The other role’s code is untouched.

common.postDatedNotice: Dated ahead — the cash side books to the post-dated account until it matures. The document is allocatable meanwhile.
common.footerNote: Tax and the inclusive total are calculated when you post. This footer shows the exclusive value of the lines you have entered.
common.outstandingTitle: Still open on the source document
common.outstandingNote: Lower a quantity or drop a line and the rest stays open. Raising one past what is left is refused on the line, because the order is where the remaining quantity is known.
common.itemLineNote: A line with an item takes its price and its account from the catalogue and moves stock; a line with only an account is a charge and moves none. Both belong on one document.
common.purchaseCodeNote: The authority requires a purchase code on a sale to a customer with a TIN. The customer gets it from their own EBM.

arInvoice.title: Invoice
arInvoice.subtitle: Customer invoice — posts to the AR control account against revenue

arCreditNote.title: Credit note
arCreditNote.subtitle: Customer credit note — reverses revenue and reduces what the customer owes

arReceipt.title: Receipt
arReceipt.subtitle: Customer receipt — allocate it to open invoices once posted

apInvoice.title: Supplier invoice
apInvoice.subtitle: Supplier invoice — posts to the AP control account against expense

apCreditNote.title: Return to supplier
apCreditNote.subtitle: Supplier debit note — reverses expense and reduces what you owe

apPayment.title: Payment
apPayment.subtitle: Supplier payment — allocate it to open invoices once posted

allocation.subtitle: Match open debits against open credits. Realized exchange differences and settlement discounts are shown before you post.
allocation.creditsHintAr: Receipts and credit notes to apply
allocation.creditsHintAp: Payments and debit notes to apply
allocation.selectPartner: Choose a partner to see their open items.
allocation.previewEmpty: Enter an amount to allocate, then preview.
allocation.previewStale: Amounts changed — preview again to see what will post.
allocation.previewFromServer: Computed by the same service that posts it, not re-derived here.
allocation.previewNoPostings: This allocation posts nothing to the ledger — it closes the open items and no more. There is no exchange difference and no discount to record.

batches.subtitleAr: Charge or credit many customers at once. Each line posts as its own journal document, ages on the customer's terms, and can be allocated like any other.
batches.subtitleAp: Charge or credit many suppliers at once. Each line posts as its own journal document, ages on the supplier's terms, and can be allocated like any other.
batches.atomicNote: One unit of work: if any line is refused — a partner on hold, a closed period — none of them post.
batches.signHintAr: A positive amount charges the customer; a negative one credits them.
batches.signHintAp: A positive amount increases what you owe the supplier; a negative one reduces it.

enquiry.subtitle: Every document against a partner, with a running balance — and a drill-down from an open item to the journal entry behind it.
enquiry.selectPartner: Choose a partner to see their account.

instruments.subtitleAr: Cheques and other instruments taken but not yet banked. Each is a real claim and can be allocated while it waits — only the cash is pending.
instruments.subtitleAp: Instruments issued but not yet cleared. Each is a real obligation and can be allocated while it waits — only the cash is pending.
instruments.none: Nothing is waiting to be banked.
instruments.nothingDue: Nothing has matured on or before this date.
instruments.explainer: Banking posts the transfer from the post-dated account to the cash account each instrument named, through the PostingEngine, dated at its maturity.
instruments.skippedWarning: {count} were due but could not be banked — check the AR/AP defaults and the cash account on each.

documentList.subtitleAr: Every posted customer document, with the way to correct one
documentList.subtitleAp: Every posted supplier document, with the way to correct one
documentList.settlementHasNoLines: A settlement carries a header amount rather than lines.
documentList.reverseDescription: Posts a mirror entry and withdraws the open item. Nothing is deleted.
documentList.reasonPlaceholder: Why this document is being reversed
documentList.reverseFailed: The document could not be reversed
documentList.noReversePermission: You do not have permission to reverse documents
documentList.unallocateDescription: Posts a mirror allocation and puts the open amount back on both documents.
documentList.unallocateFailed: The allocation could not be undone
documentList.isAnUnallocation: This row is itself an unallocation
documentList.noUnallocatePermission: You do not have permission to unallocate
documentList.fiscalRefundIrreversible: A refund cannot be refunded. The authority has no such receipt — correct this with a new invoice instead.
documentList.fiscalStatusUnresolved: The authority has not answered for this document yet. Resolve its queue row first: cancelling a row the authority is holding would leave a sale declared and unrefunded.

reports.noRows: Nothing to report for this selection.
reports.name: Name
reports.ageSubtitle: Open items bucketed at the as-of date, on the bucket set's own basis.
reports.allocSubtitle: What was matched against what, and the exchange difference it realized.
reports.listSubtitle: The partner master as it stands, with contact details and status.
reports.txSubtitle: Documents posted in the period, paged from the server.
reports.stmtSubtitle: Rendered to PDF on the job queue, then downloaded — there is no synchronous PDF.

common.name: Name
common.noPermission: You do not have permission to change this.

items.title: Inventory items
items.subtitle: The catalogue. Only stock items ever carry a quantity; service and non-stock items are here to be sold and invoiced.
items.descriptionPlaceholder: What this item is, for the picker and the invoice line
items.accountsNote: Left blank, an item posts to the company's inventory account. Cost-of-sales, sales and tax defaults are carried for P6 and do nothing yet.
items.lockedNote: Type, unit of measure and inventory account are fixed once a move has been posted against the item.
items.weightNote: Weight is only read by a landed cost split on the weight basis, which refuses a target item that has none.
items.fiscalNote: An item is registered with the authority on its first fiscal use, and re-registered under the same code whenever one of these four changes. A sale of an item with no class code is refused.

barcodes.title: Barcodes
barcodes.subtitle: Every barcode in the company, and what each one stands for. A code may name a single unit or a whole pack — the unit and pack quantity are how a scan becomes a quantity. Codes are added on the item; this is the listing, and the only place a code attached to two items would show up.
barcodes.chooseUom: Choose the unit this code means
barcodes.uniqueNote: A barcode is unique across the company, so one code can never mean two items.

warehouses.title: Warehouses
warehouses.subtitle: Where stock sits. Each warehouse belongs to a branch, and that branch is the one every move it carries posts to.
warehouses.inTransitNote: The in-transit location is created with the company and cannot be edited or chosen on a document. Stock sits here between the two legs of a transfer.

uomCategories.title: Units of measure
uomCategories.subtitle: A category is a family of units that convert to one another — Count, Weight, Volume, Length. Every unit in it is a multiple of the category's base unit.
uomCategories.baseNote: The base unit is created with its category and is always 1. Every other unit says how many base units it is worth.
uomCategories.quantityUnitNote: The authority's own quantity-unit code (§4.6), synced from the device. A fiscalized line whose unit has none is refused rather than guessed at.

defaults.title: Inventory defaults
defaults.subtitle: The accounts inventory posts to, and how the company behaves when stock runs out.
defaults.policyBlock: Block — refuse an issue that would go below zero
defaults.policyAllow: Allow — post it at the last known cost and flag it
defaults.controlNote: Inventory control and Stock in transit are control accounts: only the inventory module may post to them, and every line carries an item. Opening stock therefore comes in through an inventory journal batch, never a GL journal.
defaults.cogsNote: Cost of sales is posted by the companion stock entry of a sales invoice and by a landed cost whose target no longer holds the goods.
defaults.policyNote: Under Allow, an issue with no stock behind it is costed at the last positive average and flagged provisional. Nothing corrects it later — the flag is the review trail.

rename.title: Rename item code
rename.subtitle: The code changes; the item does not. Every move, document and journal line keeps pointing at the same item, which is why the history below survives the rename.
rename.noHistory: Nothing has changed on this item yet.
rename.safetyNote: Reports and enquiries read by code, so a rename shows up everywhere at once.

documents.serverComputed: Cost is computed by the server at posting; the figures here are estimates.
documents.title: Inventory documents
documents.subtitle: Every posted adjustment, journal batch and count variance — and the way to reverse one.
documents.reverseDescription: Posts a mirror of every line, at the values they were posted at, and leaves this document standing as reversed.
documents.reverseFailed: The reversal could not be posted
documents.alreadyReversed: This document has already been reversed
documents.noReversePermission: You do not have permission to reverse a stock document
documents.wasReversed: Reversed. The mirror document carries the entry that undid this one.

adjustments.title: Inventory adjustment
adjustments.subtitle: One item, one warehouse — posts through the PostingEngine on Post.
adjustments.valueNote: Value is unit cost × quantity for increases; decreases are costed by the server at the item's average.
adjustments.revaluationNote: A revaluation changes value only — quantity stays as it is.
adjustments.insufficientHint: Decreases cannot take the warehouse below zero.

journalBatches.title: Inventory journal batch
journalBatches.subtitle: Many lines, one unit of work — each line posts as its own document.
journalBatches.atomicNote: The batch posts as one unit: if any line is refused, none of them post.
journalBatches.posted: {count, plural, one {# document posted} other {# documents posted}}
journalBatches.unitCostHint: Unit cost is entered on increases only; decreases are costed at the warehouse average.

transfers.title: Warehouse transfers
transfers.subtitle: Move stock between warehouses at cost — in transit until received.
transfers.dispatched: {number} dispatched — receive it at the destination
transfers.nowNote: Transfer now dispatches and receives in one step; Dispatch only leaves the stock in transit until it is received.
transfers.inTransitNote: In-transit stock is held on the transit warehouse until Receive.
transfers.reverseDescription: Mirrors both legs at the values they were posted at: the stock goes back to where it came from and the in-transit account clears.
transfers.reverseFailed: The transfer could not be reversed

counts.title: Inventory counts
counts.subtitle: Snapshot the warehouse, enter counts, review variances, process.
counts.includeZero: Include items with zero on hand
counts.staleHint: Stock moved since the snapshot — re-snapshot before processing.
counts.reviewSubtitle: What Process will post — only counted lines with a difference.
counts.previewStale: Some lines are stale — re-snapshot them before processing.
counts.processedNoDocument: Session completed — no variances to post
counts.completedNote: This session has been processed; counts are read-only.

enquiry.title: Item enquiry
enquiry.subtitle: What an item holds, what it is worth, and every move behind both.
enquiry.selectItem: Choose an item to see its stock and its moves.
enquiry.noLocations: This item is not held anywhere on this date.
enquiry.oneLocationOnly: Narrowed to one warehouse. The figures above stay item-wide.
enquiry.availableNote: Committed is what open sales orders have promised from this location and On order what open purchase orders still owe it. Available is quantity less committed and is shown signed: a negative means more has been promised than is held, which the default backorder policy permits and which the sales order listing shows as a positive shortfall.
enquiry.kitHasNoPosition: A kit is a virtual bundle, never held and never committed: what a kit line promises is its component items, and it is those that show a position here. Open a component to see what the warehouse actually has to find.
enquiry.totalsNote: The totals row adds up the locations listed above, which a warehouse filter narrows. The three figures at the top of the page are item-wide as at the as-of date and do not move with the filter, so the two can legitimately differ.

reports.movementSubtitle: Opening, in, out and closing per item and warehouse over a date range.
reports.countSubtitle: Count sessions, their variances, and the document each one posted.
reports.transactionSubtitle: Every stock move in the range, with the entry it posted with.
reports.valuationSubtitle: What stock was worth on a date, and what the inventory account should read.
reports.name: Name
reports.signedOutNote: Out is shown signed, so opening + in + out = closing.

kits.sectionTitle: What this kit is made of
kits.empty: No components yet. A kit with none is refused on an order line.
kits.note: Saved as one definition, not row by row: a kit is only meaningful as a set. Editing it changes what the next order line explodes into and restates nothing already ordered.

devices.title: EBM devices
devices.subtitle: One electronic billing machine per branch, and what the authority knows about it
devices.empty: No device is registered. A company with no active device is not fiscalized, and nothing it posts is declared.
devices.registerNote: Registering records the device here. It is not declared to the authority, and issues no receipts, until it is initialized.
devices.registerFailed: The device could not be registered
devices.deviceSerialPlaceholder: The serial registered on the authority's portal
devices.keysNote: A device's keys are never shown, exported or logged: no response model has a field for one. What is shown is whether the device is holding them.
devices.activationNote: Initialize is the only way a device becomes active, and re-initializing is how a suspended one is brought back — there is no separate Activate.
devices.initializeFailed: The device could not be initialized
devices.suspendNote: A suspended device stops fiscalizing and its branch cannot invoice. Its receipts stay the authority's record; bring it back by re-initializing it.
devices.suspendFailed: The device could not be suspended
devices.syncFailed: The code tables could not be synced

tin.notFound: The authority holds no taxpayer with this number
tin.failed: The authority could not be reached
tin.noDevice: Verifying a TIN asks an active EBM device; this company has none.

document.title: Fiscalization
document.noReceiptYet: The authority has not signed this document yet. Its queue row is below.
document.retried: Row released; it will be sent next
document.retryFailed: The row could not be released
document.verified: The device was asked what it holds
document.verifyFailed: The device could not be reached
document.attachFailed: The receipt could not be attached
document.printPending: Not signed by the authority yet — the queue row is {status}. A fiscal receipt cannot be printed before the receipt number exists.
document.copyDescription: A second print is a copy: it is watermarked, it says it is not an official receipt, and the copy counter moves. Nothing is sent to the authority.
document.copyFailed: The copy could not be printed

receipt.notOfficial: THIS IS NOT AN OFFICIAL RECEIPT

queue.title: Fiscal queue
queue.subtitle: What each device is holding, in the order it will be sent
queue.noRows: Nothing is queued. Every declaration this company has made has been signed.
queue.retried: Row released; it will be sent next
queue.retryFailed: The row could not be released
queue.verified: The device was asked what it holds
queue.verifyFailed: The device could not be reached
queue.attachFailed: The receipt could not be attached
queue.rowDescription: What was sent, what came back, and who has touched it. Device keys are stripped from both.
queue.attachTitle: Attach a receipt read off MyRRA
queue.attachDescription: Key the receipt exactly as the authority's portal shows it. This is recorded as your assertion about what the authority holds, with your note.
queue.attachNotePlaceholder: Where you read these, and when

purchases.title: EBM purchases
purchases.subtitle: What other taxpayers have declared selling to this company
purchases.fetchFailed: The purchase feed could not be fetched
purchases.empty: The authority is holding no purchases for this company.
purchases.acceptFailed: The purchase could not be confirmed
purchases.rejectFailed: The purchase could not be rejected
purchases.acceptDescription: Confirming tells the authority this company accepts the purchase. Name the supplier invoice it became, if this company keyed one.
purchases.acceptNote: A supplier invoice is never registered twice: if the document you name has already queued its own registration, that row is cancelled in favour of this confirmation.

imports.title: Import declarations
imports.subtitle: What customs told the authority this company brought into the country
imports.fetchFailed: The declarations could not be fetched
imports.empty: The authority is holding no import declarations for this company.
imports.acknowledgmentNote: Approving a declared line is a compliance acknowledgment. It moves no stock and posts nothing — the goods reached the ledger through their goods receipt.
imports.approveFailed: The declaration could not be approved
imports.rejectFailed: The declaration could not be rejected
imports.approveDescription: Name the Vinea item this declared line became. The authority is asking which item code it should record against the declaration.
imports.rejectDescription: Rejecting tells the authority this company does not recognise the declared line.

common.orderNotFound: This order could not be found.

defaults.title: Order defaults
defaults.subtitle: The accounts order entry posts to, and what happens when a customer orders more than there is.
defaults.policyAllow: Allow — take the order and show the shortfall
defaults.policyBlock: Block — refuse a line that promises more than is available
defaults.accrualNote: Goods received not invoiced is a control account: only inventory and accounts payable may post to it and every line carries an item, which is what makes its balance provably the value of every receipt not yet invoiced.
defaults.clearingNote: Landed cost clearing is deliberately an ordinary account. Freight arrives on a forwarder's supplier invoice and duty as a cashbook payment to the revenue authority, and a control account would refuse both. Purchase price variance carries the difference when an invoice disagrees with the receipt it matches, on price or on rate.
defaults.policyNote: Under Allow a sales order may promise stock the warehouse does not hold, and the shortfall is shown as a backorder on the order, the enquiry and the line. Under Block the line is refused outright.
defaults.warehouseNote: The default warehouse is the inventory default, shown here because sales and purchase orders take their lines from it. Change it on Maintenance → Inventory → Defaults.
defaults.loadFailed: These settings could not be read. Seeing them needs one of the order-entry permissions; changing them needs the order-entry setup right.

salesOrders.title: Sales orders
salesOrders.subtitle: What customers have asked for, and what is still owed them. An order posts nothing — it is a promise until an invoice is raised from it.
salesOrders.backorderNote: Lines short counts the order’s lines whose warehouses cannot currently cover what is still owed on them. It moves when stock arrives or another order takes it — nothing is reserved. Open the order for how much each line is short, in its own unit.

salesOrder.title: Sales order
salesOrder.subtitle: A promise to a customer. It claims its number and posts nothing.
salesOrder.postsNothing: An order writes no journal entry and no stock move. What it holds is committed, not posted.
salesOrder.componentsNote: Indented lines are a kit's components: they are what leaves the warehouse and what the sale costs, while the parent line carries the price.
salesOrder.closeNote: What is left on this order is given up and the history stays. Nothing is posted.
salesOrder.cancelNote: Only an order with nothing invoiced can be cancelled. It keeps its number.
salesOrder.transitionFailed: The order could not be changed
salesOrder.linesNote: A kit is one line here. Its components are exploded when the order is saved, and Breakup edits them afterwards.
salesOrder.resetNote: These lines were broken up by hand and their quantity has changed. Saving re-explodes them from the catalogue definition, and the substitutions that were keyed in go with it.

breakup.title: Breakup — {item}
breakup.subtitle: What ships in this order's box, for {quantity} of them. These are delivery quantities, not per-kit rates.
breakup.note: This edits one order. The catalogue definition is what the next kit line explodes from, and orders already taken keep the lines they were keyed with.

purchaseOrders.title: Purchase orders
purchaseOrders.subtitle: What has been ordered from suppliers, and how much of it has arrived. An order posts nothing — the goods receipt does.
purchaseOrders.noBackorderNote: There is no backordered column here. A backorder is what a customer was promised and the shelf cannot cover; what a purchase order is short of is simply what the supplier has not delivered, which the status and each line's remaining already say.

purchaseOrder.title: Purchase order
purchaseOrder.subtitle: A commitment to a supplier. It claims its number and posts nothing.
purchaseOrder.postsNothing: An order writes no journal entry and no stock move. The receipt is what posts the accrual.
purchaseOrder.linesNote: A kit cannot be bought — only its parts. Service lines are received by their invoice, never by a goods receipt.
purchaseOrder.noStockLines: Nothing on this order is received into stock.
purchaseOrder.noServiceLines: This order has no open service lines to invoice.
purchaseOrder.closeNote: What is left on this order is given up and the history stays. Nothing is posted.
purchaseOrder.cancelNote: Only an order with nothing received can be cancelled. It keeps its number.
purchaseOrder.transitionFailed: The order could not be changed
purchaseOrder.resetNote: These lines were broken up by hand and their quantity has changed. Saving re-explodes them from the catalogue definition.

goodsReceived.title: Goods received
goodsReceived.subtitle: Every receipt, what it was valued at, and how much of it an invoice has since claimed.
goodsReceived.statusNote: The three states are shown the way Evolution names them. A receipt nothing has been invoiced against is Unprocessed, one an invoice has partly claimed is Confirmed, and one fully claimed is Processed; the stored values are received, partially_matched and matched.
goodsReceived.accrualNote: The unmatched total is over the whole filtered set rather than this page, because it exists to be compared with the Goods received not invoiced account. A page total could not be.

goodsReceipt.title: New goods receipt
goodsReceipt.subtitle: Goods that arrived. This posts: stock in at what the delivery note says, against goods received not invoiced.
goodsReceipt.fromOrderSubtitle: Prepared from a purchase order. Lower a quantity or drop a line; what is left stays on the order.
goodsReceipt.postFailed: The receipt could not be posted
goodsReceipt.prepareFailed: The purchase order could not be prepared for receipt
goodsReceipt.postsNote: A receipt values stock at what was keyed. The invoice that follows relieves the accrual, and any disagreement on price goes to purchase price variance.
goodsReceipt.linesNote: Matched is the quantity a supplier invoice has claimed against this receipt. What is left unmatched is what the accrual still carries.
goodsReceipt.outstandingNote: Receive less than this and the rest stays on the order. Receiving more is refused on the line, because the order is where the remaining quantity is known.
goodsReceipt.nothingToInvoice: There is nothing left on this receipt for an invoice to claim.
goodsReceipt.matchedCannotReverse: An invoice has already claimed part of this receipt — reverse that invoice first.
goodsReceipt.alreadyReversed: This receipt has already been reversed.
goodsReceipt.reverseNote: The goods go back out at the value they came in at, and a reversing entry is posted. Nothing is edited or deleted.
goodsReceipt.reverseFailed: The receipt could not be reversed

landedCosts.title: Landed costs
landedCosts.subtitle: Costs incurred for goods — freight, duty, clearing — spread into what those goods are worth.
landedCosts.note: There is no draft state: a landed cost is computed and posted in one step, and the only other state it can be in is reversed.

landedCost.subtitle: Spread a cost into the goods it was incurred for. See the shares before anything posts.
landedCost.previewFailed: The shares could not be computed
landedCost.postFailed: The landed cost could not be posted
landedCost.postsNote: Post writes one entry: the clearing account out, stock value in, and any share with no stock left to carry it goes to cost of sales.
landedCost.targetsTitle: What the cost is being spread over
landedCost.noTargets: Add a goods receipt to choose the lines this cost belongs to.
landedCost.previewNote: A share marked cost of sales is one whose location holds none of the item, so there is no stock value left to add it to. Whether that is still true is settled under the costing lock when the cost is posted, which is why this says would rather than will.
landedCost.cogsNote: A line that went to cost of sales has no stock move: the goods had already left the location, and holding the cost back until they came back would mean holding it for ever.
landedCost.alreadyReversed: This landed cost has already been reversed.
landedCost.reverseNote: The allocation comes back out at the values it went in at, and a reversing entry is posted. Nothing is edited or deleted.
landedCost.reverseFailed: The landed cost could not be reversed

breakupScreen.title: Breakup
breakupScreen.subtitle: What ships in one order’s box. Choose an open sales order and a kit line on it.
breakupScreen.chooseFirst: Choose a sales order to see the kit lines on it.
breakupScreen.noKits: This order has no kit lines.
breakupScreen.note: Only open orders are offered. What has been invoiced has shipped, and no edit here reaches the lines it went out on.

orderEnquiry.salesSubtitle: What was promised on one order, what has been invoiced against it, and what is still owed.
orderEnquiry.purchaseSubtitle: What was ordered from one supplier, what has arrived, and what is still on its way.
orderEnquiry.chooseFirst: Choose an order to see its lines and the documents raised against it.
orderEnquiry.linesNote: Ordered, invoiced, received and remaining are counted in each item's base unit and are queries over the documents that fulfilled the line, never stored columns — a reversal moves them by construction. Backordered is the part of what is left that the warehouse cannot currently cover; a kit's components are indented under the line the customer saw, because it is the components the warehouse has to find.
orderEnquiry.noDocuments: Nothing has been raised against this order yet.
orderEnquiry.documentsNote: A stock-bearing document posts two entries — the partner side and the companion stock entry — and both are linked here, because an enquiry offering only the receivable would drill past the cost of the sale. A reversed document stays in this list, struck through: what happened to this order includes the invoice that was raised and taken back, and its quantity is what that document keyed rather than a net contribution. The quantity column sums base units across the document's lines, so it is only meaningful where those lines share a unit; the per-line figures above are the ones to read.

orderReport.salesSubtitle: Order lines and what each still owes the customer.
orderReport.purchaseSubtitle: Order lines and what each supplier still owes.
orderReport.outstandingOnlyLabel: Outstanding lines only — open orders with something still to come
orderReport.totalsNote: Deliberately subtotals rather than totals. Three kilograms and two crates do not add up to five of anything, and an order's exchange rate is display only — stock is never valued at it — so there is no rate here that could put two currencies on one line either. The count of lines is the total that always means something, and all three are taken over every line the filters select rather than over this page.

goodsReceivedReport.title: Goods received
goodsReceivedReport.subtitle: Receipts, what each was valued at, and how much of it still sits in the accrual.
goodsReceivedReport.accrualTie: This total is the balance of account 2350 at the same date — Σ (received − relieved) over every receipt the filters select, which is what makes the control account provable from a screen rather than only from a test.

landedCostReport.title: Landed cost
landedCostReport.subtitle: What each consignment actually cost, allocation by allocation, per receipt line.
landedCostReport.clearingNote: The clearing account holds what has been booked to it less what has been allocated out of it, so it reads zero once every cost booked there has been spread. Shares are base currency, which is the currency the account holds.
landedCostReport.grainNote: One row per receipt line, not per allocation: a single freight bill routinely covers consignments from several suppliers, and only this grain answers what a given consignment cost.
landedCostReport.noQuantityTotalNote: Quantity then is what the location held when the share was struck, in each item's own base unit — rows across items are in different units, so the column is not totalled. A share that went to cost of sales moved no stock at all: the location held none of the item, and the share still had to leave the clearing account.

vatReturn.title: VAT return
vatReturn.subtitle: The return over a range, and the movement on the VAT accounts it accounts for
vatReturn.noFigures: Nothing has been posted in this range.
vatReturn.salesStandardVat: VAT on sales at the standard rate
vatReturn.purchasesStandardVat: VAT on purchases at the standard rate
vatReturn.tieNote: This return is reconciled, not balanced: each VAT account's movement is shown beside what the return declares of it, and every journal line making up the rest is listed. A VAT payment to the authority, or a journal keyed without a tax code, belongs in that list rather than in a rounding.
vatReturn.lateEntriesNote: Posted into a range that has already been filed. A filed return never changes, so these are declared here instead.
vatReturn.fileDescription: Filing freezes these figures and posts the settlement entry through the ledger.
vatReturn.fileNote: The figures as filed never change. An entry posted into this range afterwards lands on the next return under Late entries.
vatReturn.fileFailed: The return could not be filed
vatReturn.noneFiled: No return has been filed for this company.
vatReturn.detailDescription: The figures as they were submitted — read back from the snapshot, never recomputed.
vatReturn.reverseReasonPlaceholder: Why this return is being reopened
vatReturn.reverseFailed: The return could not be reversed
